subject: english-literature
title: Marxist and Feminist Lenses
welcome_lead: Critical theory expands close reading. Marxist and feminist lenses ask what the text reveals about class and gender.
meta_desc: English Literature: Marxist and feminist critical approaches.
final_note: Every reading is political — make yours conscious.

concepts.def: Reading literature in terms of class, ideology and material conditions.
Marx's distinction between economic foundation and cultural forms.
The system of ideas that naturalises a social order.
Analysis of how texts represent and shape gender.
Elaine Showalter's term for the study of women writers and female literary traditions.
Helene Cixous's call for a writing rooted in the female body and difference.

walkthroughs.body_html: Terry Eagleton argues literature both reflects and shapes ideology. Reading Mansfield Park with Eagleton foregrounds the silent slave economy behind Sir Thomas's wealth.
Showalter divides women's writing into Feminine (imitation), Feminist (protest), Female (self-discovery). The schema offers a framework for tracing women's literary tradition.
Cixous urges women to 'write the body'. Whether you accept the essentialism, the move opens new questions about how language is gendered.

mcqs.q: What are conventions of the Gothic genre?
options: Gothic just means scary stories with vampires and ghosts.
Gothic refers to medieval architecture, not literature.
Settings of ruin and decay, supernatural or psychological terror, transgression of boundaries, the sublime, doubled or haunted protagonists, and atmospheric excess.
Context is required because all texts are about history.

mcqs.q: What is the function of dystopian fiction?
options: Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
Dystopian fiction is just storytelling set in scary futures.
Gothic refers to medieval architecture, not literature.
To critique tendencies in the writer's own society by extrapolating them into a nightmarish future — dystopias hold up a warning mirror to the present.

mcqs.q: Why does historical context matter when reading literature?
options: Context just means writing about what the author had for breakfast.
Texts emerge from and respond to specific historical conditions — context illuminates references, assumptions and arguments that might otherwise be invisible.
Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
Context is required because all texts are about history.
